title.zh: 卷一百九十四下 列傳第一百四十四下: 突厥下
title.raw: 卷一百九十四下 列傳第一百四十四下: 突厥下 Volume 194 Biographies 144: Tujie 2

sentences.zh: 西突厥本與北突厥同祖。

translations.literal: The Western Turks originally shared the same ancestry as the Northern Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks were originally of the same stock as the Northern Turks.

sentences.zh: 初，木桿與沙缽略可汗有隙，因分為二。

translations.literal: At first Mughan and Qaghan Ishbara had a rift, and thus they split into two.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Mughan and Qaghan Ishbara fell out, and the people divided into two branches.

sentences.zh: 其國即烏孫之故地，東至突厥國，西至雷翥海，南至疏勒，北至瀚海，在長安北七千里。

translations.literal: Their state was the former territory of the Wusun; east to the Turk state, west to the Ray-chu Sea, south to Shule, north to the Hanhai, seven thousand li north of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm lay on the old lands of the Wusun, bounded on the east by the Turk domains, on the west by the Ray-chu Sea, on the south by Shule, and on the north by the Hanhai, seven thousand li north of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 自焉耆國西北七日行，至其南庭；

translations.literal: From Yanqi, traveling northwest for seven days, one reaches its southern court;
translations.idiomatic: From Yanqi it is a seven-day journey northwest to their southern court;

sentences.zh: 又正北八日行，至其北庭。

translations.literal: Again, traveling due north for eight days, one reaches its northern court.
translations.idiomatic: Another eight days' travel due north brings one to their northern court.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒、龜茲及西域諸胡國，皆歸附之。

translations.literal: The Tiele, Kucha, and the various Hu states of the Western Regions all submitted to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele, Kucha, and the various Hu states of the Western Regions all submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 其人雜有都陸及弩失畢、歌邏祿、處月、處密，伊吾等諸種。

translations.literal: Their people were a mixture of the Dulü, Nushibi, Qarluk, Chuyue, Chumi, Yiwu, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Their population included the Dulü, Nushibi, Qarluk, Chuyue, Chumi, Yiwu, and other peoples.

sentences.zh: 風俗大抵與突厥同，唯言語微差。

translations.literal: Their customs were largely the same as the Turks', only their speech differed slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were much the same as those of the Turks, with only slight differences in language.

sentences.zh: 其官有葉護，有特勒，常以可汗子弟及宗族為之；

translations.literal: Their offices included yabghu and tegin, usually filled by sons of the qaghan and members of the royal clan;
translations.idiomatic: They had offices such as yabghu and tegin, usually held by the qaghan's sons and kinsmen;

sentences.zh: 又有乙斤、屈利啜、閻洪達、頡利發、吐屯、俟斤等官，皆代襲其位。

translations.literal: There were also the offices of yijin, qulicuo, yan hongda, jielifa, tutun, and yijin, all of which were inherited in succession.
translations.idiomatic: There were also yijin, qulicuo, yan hongda, jielifa, tutun, and yijin posts, all inherited in turn.

sentences.zh: 處羅可汗，隋煬帝大業中與其弟闕達設及特勒大奈入朝。

translations.literal: Qaghan Chuluo, in the Daye era of Emperor Yang of Sui, came to court with his younger brother Quedashi and Tegin Dana.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yang's Daye reign, Qaghan Chuluo came to court with his younger brother Quedashi and Tegin Dana.

sentences.zh: 仍從煬帝征高麗，賜號為曷薩那可汗。

translations.literal: He still followed Emperor Yang on the campaign against Goguryeo and was granted the title He-sa-na Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Yang against Goguryeo and was given the title He-sa-na Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 遇江都之亂，從宇文化及至河北。

translations.literal: When the Jiangdu coup occurred, he followed Yuwen Huaji to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil broke out at Jiangdu, he followed Yuwen Huaji into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，歸長安，高祖為之降榻，引與同坐，封歸義郡王。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, he returned to Chang'an; Gaozu lowered his couch for him, drew him to sit together, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Guiyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji's defeat he returned to Chang'an; Gaozu lowered his couch, seated him beside himself, and enfeoffed him Prince of Guiyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 獻大珠於高祖。

translations.literal: He presented a great pearl to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He presented a great pearl to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖勞之曰：「珠信為寶，朕所重者赤心，珠無所用。

translations.literal: Gaozu comforted him, saying: "Pearls are indeed treasure, but what I value is a loyal heart; pearls are of no use to me.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu reassured him: "Pearls may be precious, but what I value is your loyal heart; pearls are useless to me.

sentences.zh: 」竟不受之。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused them.

sentences.zh: 先與始畢有隙，及在京師，始畢遣使請殺之，高祖不許。

translations.literal: He had earlier had a feud with Shibi; when he was in the capital, Shibi sent envoys requesting his execution, but Gaozu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been at odds with Shibi; while he was in the capital Shibi sent envoys asking that he be killed, but Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 群臣諫曰：「今若不與，則是存一人而失一國也，後必為患。

translations.literal: The ministers remonstrated, saying: "If you do not grant this now, you will preserve one man but lose one state; later this must become a trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged: "If you refuse now, you save one man but lose a whole state; trouble will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「人窮來歸我，殺之不義。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "When a man in extremity comes to submit to us, to kill him is unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "A man who comes to us in desperation should not be killed; that would be unjust.

sentences.zh: 」驟諫於高祖，由是遲回者久之。

translations.literal: He remonstrated sharply with Gaozu, and because of this Gaozu hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed his counsel on Gaozu again and again, and Gaozu wavered for a long time.

sentences.zh: 不得已，乃引曷薩那於內殿，與之縱酒，既而送至中書省，縱北突厥使殺之。

translations.literal: Unable to do otherwise, he then led He-sa-na into the inner hall, drank freely with him, and afterward sent him to the Secretariat, allowing the Northern Turk envoys to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: At last, with no other choice, he brought He-sa-na into the inner hall and drank with him, then sent him to the Secretariat and let the Northern Turk envoys kill him.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，令以禮改葬。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, he ordered that He-sa-na be reburied according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong took the throne, he ordered a proper reburial for him.

sentences.zh: 闕達設初居於會寧，有部落三千余騎。

translations.literal: Quedashi at first dwelt at Huining, with a tribe of more than three thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Quedashi had first lived at Huining with a following of more than three thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 至隋末，自稱闕達可汗。

translations.literal: By the end of Sui he styled himself Qaghan Queda.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui he proclaimed himself Qaghan Queda.

sentences.zh: 武德初，遣使內屬，拜吐烏過拔闕可汗，厚加撫慰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he sent envoys to submit; he was appointed Qaghan Tuwu Guo Ba Que and richly comforted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he sent envoys to swear allegiance; he was named Qaghan Tuwu Guo Ba Que and treated with great favor.

sentences.zh: 尋為李軌所滅。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was destroyed by Li Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was destroyed by Li Gui.

sentences.zh: 特勒大奈，隋大業中與曷薩那可汗同歸中國。

translations.literal: Tegin Dana, in the Daye era of Sui, returned to China together with He-sa-na Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Tegin Dana, during Sui's Daye reign, came to China together with He-sa-na Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 及從煬帝討遼東，以功授金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When he followed Emperor Yang against Liaodong, he was appointed Jinzi Guanglu Grand Master for merit.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Emperor Yang against Liaodong, he was made Jinzi Guanglu Grand Master for his service.

sentences.zh: 後分其部落於樓煩。

translations.literal: Later his tribe was divided and settled at Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: Later his tribe was divided and settled at Loufan.

sentences.zh: 會高祖舉兵，大奈率其眾以從。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised his army, Dana led his followers to join him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised his army, Dana led his men to follow him.

sentences.zh: 隋將桑顯和襲義軍於飲馬泉，諸軍多已奔退，大奈將數百騎出顯和後，掩其不備，擊，大破之，諸軍復振。

translations.literal: The Sui general Sang Xianhe attacked the righteous army at Yinma Spring; most of the army had already fled, but Dana led several hundred horsemen out behind Xianhe, took him unawares, struck, and routed him greatly, and the armies rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui general Sang Xianhe struck the loyalist army at Yinma Spring and most troops had already broken, Dana led several hundred horsemen around behind Xianhe, caught him off guard, and routed him, rallying the army.

sentences.zh: 拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 及平京城，以力戰功，賞物五千段，賜姓史氏。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, for fighting merit he was rewarded with five thousand bolts of goods and granted the surname Shi.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was taken, he received five thousand bolts of goods for valor and was granted the surname Shi.

sentences.zh: 武德初，從太宗破薛舉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he followed Taizong in defeating Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he followed Taizong in defeating Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 又從平王世充，破竇建德、劉黑闥，並有殊功。

translations.literal: He also followed in pacifying Wang Shichong and in defeating Dou Jiande and Liu Heita, each time with outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped pacify Wang Shichong and defeat Dou Jiande and Liu Heita, winning distinction each time.

sentences.zh: 賜宮女三人，雜彩萬余段。

translations.literal: He was given three palace women and more than ten thousand bolts of mixed silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was given three palace women and more than ten thousand bolts of mixed silks.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，累遷右武衛大將軍、檢校豐州都督，封竇國公，實封三百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he rose in succession to General of the Right Martial Guard and acting Protector-General of Fengzhou, was enfeoffed Duke of Dou with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 he became General of the Right Martial Guard and acting Protector-General of Fengzhou, was made Duke of Dou with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，贈輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; posthumously he was made Supporting-the-State General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died and was posthumously made Supporting-the-State General.

sentences.zh: 初，曷薩那之朝隋也，為煬帝所拘，其國人遂立薩那之叔父，曰射匱可汗。

translations.literal: At first, when He-sa-na came to court at Sui, Emperor Yang detained him; his countrymen then set up He-sa-na's uncle, called Qaghan Shekui.
translations.idiomatic: When He-sa-na had come to the Sui court, Emperor Yang detained him; his people then set up his uncle as Qaghan Shekui.

sentences.zh: 射匱可汗者，達頭可汗之孫也。

translations.literal: Qaghan Shekui was the grandson of Qaghan Tatou.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Shekui was the grandson of Qaghan Tatou.

sentences.zh: 既立後，始開土宇，東至金山，西至海，自玉門已西諸國皆役屬之。

translations.literal: After he was established, he first opened his territory: east to Mount Jin, west to the sea; from Yumen westward all states were made to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he expanded his domain east to Mount Jin and west to the sea; from Yumen westward every state submitted.

sentences.zh: 遂與北突厥為敵，乃建庭於龜茲北三彌山，尋卒。

translations.literal: He then became enemy to the Northern Turks, built his court north of Kucha at Mount Sanmi, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He made himself the Northern Turks' enemy, built his court north of Kucha at Mount Sanmi, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 弟統葉護可汗代立。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qaghan Tong Yehu succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qaghan Tong Yehu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 統葉護可汗，勇而有謀，善攻戰。

translations.literal: Qaghan Tong Yehu was brave and resourceful, skilled in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Tong Yehu was brave and shrewd, skilled in war.

sentences.zh: 遂北並鐵勒，西拒波斯，南接罽賓，悉歸之。

translations.literal: He then annexed the Tiele in the north, held off Persia in the west, reached Jibin in the south, and all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He absorbed the Tiele in the north, held Persia at bay in the west, reached Jibin in the south, and brought them all under his rule.

sentences.zh: 控弦數十萬，霸有西域，據舊烏孫之地。

translations.literal: He controlled several hundred thousand bowmen, dominated the Western Regions, and held the old Wusun lands.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded several hundred thousand bowmen, dominated the Western Regions, and held the old Wusun territory.

sentences.zh: 又移庭於石國北之千泉。

translations.literal: He also moved his court to the Thousand Springs north of Shiguo.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his court to the Thousand Springs north of Shiguo.

sentences.zh: 其西域諸國王悉授頡利發，並遣吐屯一人監統之，督其征賦。

translations.literal: All the kings of the Western Region states were given the rank jielifa, and one tutun was sent to oversee each, supervising their levies.
translations.idiomatic: Every king of the western states was given the rank jielifa, and a tutun was posted to each to supervise tribute.

sentences.zh: 西戎之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: Never had the western barbarians been so strong.
translations.idiomatic: The western peoples had never been so powerful.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，遣使貢條支巨卵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he sent envoys presenting giant eggs from Tiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 he sent envoys with giant eggs from Tiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 時北突厥作患，高祖厚加撫結，與之並力以圖北蕃，統葉護許以五年冬。

translations.literal: At that time the Northern Turks were causing trouble; Gaozu treated him generously and joined forces with him against the northern frontier; Tong Yehu promised the winter of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: While the Northern Turks were raiding, Gaozu courted him and planned a joint strike on the north; Tong Yehu promised troops by winter of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 大軍將發，頡利可汗聞之，大懼，復與統葉護通和，無相征伐。

translations.literal: When the great army was about to march, Qaghan Jieli heard of it, was greatly afraid, and made peace again with Tong Yehu; there was no mutual campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: When the expedition was ready, Qaghan Jieli, alarmed, reconciled with Tong Yehu and the two ceased fighting.

sentences.zh: 統葉護尋遣使來請婚。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu soon sent envoys requesting a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu soon sent envoys to request a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂侍臣曰：「西突厥去我懸遠，急疾不相得力，今請婚，其計安在？

translations.literal: Gaozu said to his attendants: "The Western Turks are far from us and cannot aid us quickly; now they ask for marriage—what is their plan?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked his court: "The Western Turks are distant and cannot help us in an emergency; why do they seek marriage now?

sentences.zh: 」封德彜對曰：「當今之務，莫若遠交而近攻，正可權許其婚，以威北狄。

translations.literal: Feng Deyi replied: "The urgent task today is to befriend those far and attack those near; we may provisionally grant the marriage to overawe the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi answered: "Our policy should be to court distant powers and strike nearby foes; we may grant the marriage for now to intimidate the northern Turks.

sentences.zh: 待之數年後，中國盛全，徐思其宜。

translations.literal: Wait several years until China is fully secure, then consider what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: In a few years, when the empire is fully secure, we can decide what is best.

sentences.zh: 」高祖遂許之婚，令高平王道立至其國，統葉護大悅。

translations.literal: Gaozu then promised the marriage and sent Prince of Gaoping Li Daoli to his state; Tong Yehu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu agreed to the match and sent Prince of Gaoping Li Daoli; Tong Yehu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 遇頡利可汗頻歲入寇，西蕃路梗，由是未果為婚。

translations.literal: But Qaghan Jieli raided year after year, the western routes were blocked, and therefore the marriage was never concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli kept raiding, the western roads were cut, and the marriage never took place.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，遣真珠統俟斤與高平王道立來獻萬釘寶鈿金帶，馬五千匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, True Pearl, the yijin of the tribes, came with Li Daoli, Prince of Gaoping, presenting a belt studded with ten thousand nails of precious gold and five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 True Pearl, the tribal yijin, came with Prince of Gaoping Li Daoli, offering a belt of ten thousand gold nail studs and five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 時統葉護自負強盛，無恩於國，部眾鹹怨，歌邏祿種多叛之。

translations.literal: At that time Tong Yehu, relying on his strength, showed no kindness to the state; his followers all resented him, and many of the Qarluk clans rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu, confident in his power, treated the court without grace; his people resented him and many Qarluk tribes rebelled.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗不悅中國與之和親，數遣兵入寇，又遣人謂統葉護曰：「汝若迎唐家公主，要須經我國中而過。

translations.literal: Qaghan Jieli disliked China's peace with him and repeatedly sent troops to raid; he also sent men to tell Tong Yehu: "If you welcome the Tang princess, you must pass through our country.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli resented the Tang alliance and raided repeatedly; he also told Tong Yehu: "If you take a Tang princess, she must pass through our lands.

sentences.zh: 」統葉護患之，未克婚。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu was troubled by this and could not complete the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu, worried by this, could not complete the marriage.

sentences.zh: 為其伯父所殺而自立，是為莫賀咄侯屈利俟毗可汗。

translations.literal: He was killed by his uncle, who set himself up; this was Qaghan Mohe Duo Hou Qu Li Houpi.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle killed him and seized the throne as Qaghan Mohe Duo Hou Qu Li Houpi.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞統葉護之死，甚悼之，遣賫玉帛至其死所祭而焚之。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of Tong Yehu's death he mourned deeply and sent jade and silks to his place of death to sacrifice and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Tong Yehu's death, Taizong grieved and sent jade and silks to be burned at the place where he died.

sentences.zh: 會其國亂，不果至而止。

translations.literal: But his state fell into disorder and the mission could not reach there; it stopped short.
translations.idiomatic: Civil war broke out and the envoys never arrived.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄侯屈利俟毗可汗，先分統突厥種類為小可汗，及此自稱大可汗，國人不附。

translations.literal: Qaghan Mohe Duo Hou Qu Li Houpi had earlier ruled one Turk tribe as a lesser qaghan; when he now styled himself great qaghan, the people would not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe Duo had ruled a lesser qaghanate; when he proclaimed himself great qaghan his people would not obey.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢部共推泥孰莫賀設為可汗，泥孰不從。

translations.literal: The Nushibi clans together pushed Niqi Mohe She to be qaghan, but Niqi refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Nushibi clans tried to make Niqi Mohe She qaghan, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 時統葉護之子咥力特勒避莫賀咄之難，亡在康居，泥孰遂迎而立之，是為乙毗缽羅肆葉護可汗。

translations.literal: At that time Tong Yehu's son Toli Tegin, fleeing Mohe Duo's persecution, had taken refuge in Kangju; Niqi then welcomed and enthroned him as Qaghan Yipi Boluo Siyehu.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu's son Toli Tegin, fleeing Mohe Duo, hid in Kangju; Niqi welcomed him and enthroned him as Qaghan Yipi Boluo Siyehu.

sentences.zh: 連兵不息，俱遣使來朝，各請婚於我。

translations.literal: War did not cease; both sent envoys to court, each asking for marriage with us.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting continued; both sent envoys to court, each seeking a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 太宗答之曰：「汝國擾亂，君臣未定，戰爭不息，何得言婚！

translations.literal: Taizong answered them: "Your state is in turmoil, ruler and subjects unsettled, war unceasing—how can you speak of marriage!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied: "Your realm is torn by strife, your rulers unsettled, and war unending—how can you ask for marriage!"

sentences.zh: 」竟不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused them both.

sentences.zh: 仍諷令各保所部，無相征伐。

translations.literal: He still admonished them to each keep their own territory and not attack one another.
translations.idiomatic: He urged each side to hold its own lands and cease fighting.

sentences.zh: 其西域諸國及鐵勒先役屬於西突厥者，悉叛之，國內虛耗。

translations.literal: The western states and the Tiele that had earlier been subject to the Western Turks all rebelled, and the state was drained.
translations.idiomatic: Every western state and Tiele tribe that had served the Western Turks rebelled, leaving the realm hollow.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護既是舊主之子，為眾心所歸，其西面都陸可汗及莫賀咄可汗部豪帥，多來附之。

translations.literal: Siyehu, as the former ruler's son, was where popular sentiment lay; the western yabghu and Mohe Duo's tribal chiefs mostly came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: As the old qaghan's son, Siyehu commanded loyalty; western yabghus and Mohe Duo's chiefs largely joined him.

sentences.zh: 又興兵以擊莫賀咄，大敗之。

translations.literal: He also raised troops to attack Mohe Duo and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against Mohe Duo and defeated him soundly.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄遁於金山，尋為咄陸可汗所害，國人乃奉肆葉護為大可汗。

translations.literal: Mohe Duo fled to Mount Jin; soon he was killed by Qaghan Zhuolu, and the people then upheld Siyehu as great qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe Duo fled to Mount Jin; Zhuolu Qaghan soon killed him, and the people upheld Siyehu.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護可汗立，大發兵北征鐵勒，薛延陀逆擊之，反為所敗。

translations.literal: When Qaghan Siyehu was established, he launched a great campaign north against the Tiele; the Xueyantuo met him and struck back, and he was defeated in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Siyehu marched north against the Tiele; the Xueyantuo counterattacked and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護性猜狠信讒，無統馭之略。

translations.literal: Siyehu was suspicious, cruel, and believed slander; he had no talent for ruling.
translations.idiomatic: Siyehu was suspicious and cruel, trusting slander, and lacked the art of rule.

sentences.zh: 有乙利可汗者，於肆葉護功最多，由是授小可汗，以非罪族滅之。

translations.literal: There was a Yili Qaghan who had done the most for Siyehu; for this he was made a lesser qaghan, then on a false charge his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Yili Qaghan had served Siyehu best; rewarded with a lesser qaghanate, he was then destroyed on a false charge.

sentences.zh: 群下震駭，莫能自固。

translations.literal: The subordinates were shaken and none could feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: His followers were terrified and none felt safe.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護素憚泥孰，而陰欲圖之，泥孰遂適焉耆。

translations.literal: Siyehu had long feared Niqi and secretly plotted against him; Niqi then went to Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Siyehu had long feared Niqi and plotted against him; Niqi withdrew to Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 其後沒卑達幹與突厥弩失畢二部豪帥潛謀擊之，肆葉護以輕騎遁於康居，尋卒。

translations.literal: Later Meibida Gan and the chiefs of the Nushibi and Turk tribes secretly plotted against him; Siyehu fled on light horse to Kangju and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Meibida Gan and Nushibi chiefs conspired against him; Siyehu fled lightly to Kangju and soon died.

sentences.zh: 國人迎泥孰於焉耆而立之，是為咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: The people welcomed Niqi from Yanqi and enthroned him; this was Qaghan Zhuolu.
translations.idiomatic: The people brought Niqi back from Yanqi as Qaghan Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗泥孰者，亦稱大渡可汗。

translations.literal: Qaghan Zhuolu Niqi was also called Qaghan Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Zhuolu Niqi was also known as Qaghan Dadu.

sentences.zh: 父莫賀設，本隸統葉護。

translations.literal: His father Mohe She had originally been subordinate to Tong Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mohe She had served under Tong Yehu.

sentences.zh: 武德中，嘗至京師。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he once came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude he visited the capital.

sentences.zh: 時太宗居籓，務加懷輯，與之結盟為兄弟。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong was still a prince; he treated Niqi with special favor and swore brotherhood with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong was still heir apparent, he treated Niqi warmly and swore brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 既被推為可汗，遣使詣闕請降。

translations.literal: Once he was made qaghan, he sent envoys to the court requesting submission.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he sent envoys to request submission.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使賜以名號及鼓纛。

translations.literal: Taizong sent envoys granting him a title and drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent envoys with a title, drums, and banners.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，遣鴻臚少卿劉善因至其國，冊授為吞阿婁拔奚利邲咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception Liu Shanyin went to his state and invested him as Qaghan Tun A Lou Ba Xi Li Zhuolu.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 7 Vice Director Liu Shanyin invested him Qaghan Tun A Lou Ba Xi Li Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 明年，泥孰卒，其弟同娥設立，是為沙缽羅咥利失可汗。

translations.literal: The next year Niqi died; his younger brother Tong E She succeeded as Qaghan Shaboluo Xieli Shi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Niqi died; his brother Tong E She became Qaghan Shaboluo Xieli Shi.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅咥利失可汗，以貞觀九年上表請婚，獻馬五百疋。

translations.literal: Qaghan Shaboluo Xieli Shi, in the ninth year of Zhenguan, memorialized requesting marriage and presented five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 9 Shaboluo Xieli Shi asked for marriage and sent five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 朝廷唯厚加撫慰，未許其婚。

translations.literal: The court only comforted him generously and did not grant the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The court treated him generously but refused the marriage.

sentences.zh: 俄而其國分為十部，每部令一人統之，號為十設。

translations.literal: Soon his state was divided into ten divisions, each put under one man; these were called the Ten Shad.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his realm split into ten divisions, each under one leader—the Ten Shad.

sentences.zh: 每設賜以一箭，故稱十箭焉。

translations.literal: Each shad was given one arrow, hence they were called the Ten Arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Each shad received one arrow, whence the name Ten Arrows.

sentences.zh: 又分十箭為左右廂，一廂各置五箭。

translations.literal: The ten arrows were further divided into left and right wings, each wing holding five arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The ten arrows were split into left and right wings of five arrows each.

sentences.zh: 其左廂號五咄六部落，置五大啜，一啜管一箭；

translations.literal: The left wing was called the five Zhuolu tribes, with five great juelu, each juelu governing one arrow;
translations.idiomatic: The left wing comprised the five Zhuolu tribes under five great juelu, one arrow each;

sentences.zh: 其右廂號為五弩失畢，置五大俟斤，一俟斤管一箭，都號為十箭。

translations.literal: the right wing was called the five Nushibi, with five great yijin, each yijin governing one arrow; together they were called the Ten Arrows.
translations.idiomatic: the right wing comprised the five Nushibi under five great yijin, one arrow each—the whole known as the Ten Arrows.

sentences.zh: 其後或稱一箭為一部落，大箭頭為大首領。

translations.literal: Later one arrow was also called one tribe, and the head of the great arrow was the great chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Later each arrow came to mean a tribe, and the great arrow-head was the great chieftain.

sentences.zh: 五咄六部落居於碎葉已東，五弩失畢部落居於碎葉已西，自是都號為十姓部落。

translations.literal: The five Zhuolu tribes dwelt east of Suyab; the five Nushibi tribes west of Suyab; from then on all were called the Ten Surname Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The five Zhuolu lived east of Suyab and the five Nushibi west of it; thereafter all were known as the Ten Surname Tribes.

sentences.zh: 咥利失既不為眾所歸，部眾攜貳，為其統吐屯所襲，麾下亡散。

translations.literal: Xieli Shi was not followed by the masses; his followers wavered, and he was attacked by his supervising tutun; his followers scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli Shi won no loyalty; his people split, his tutun attacked him, and his forces dispersed.

sentences.zh: 咥利失以左右百余騎拒之，戰數合，統吐屯不利而去。

translations.literal: Xieli Shi resisted with a hundred-odd horsemen on his left and right; after several engagements the supervising tutun withdrew at a disadvantage.
translations.idiomatic: With barely a hundred riders he fought several rounds until the tutun broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 咥利失奔其弟步利設，與保焉耆。

translations.literal: Xieli Shi fled to his younger brother Buli She and took refuge in Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to his brother Buli She and held Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 其阿悉吉闕俟斤與統吐屯等召國人，將立欲谷設為大可汗。

translations.literal: The yijin Asijiji Que and the supervising tutun and others summoned the people, intending to set up Yugu She as great qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Asijiji Que yijin, the tutun, and others called the tribes to make Yugu She great qaghan.

sentences.zh: 以咥利失為小可汗。

translations.literal: Xieli Shi was made a lesser qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli Shi was reduced to lesser qaghan.

sentences.zh: 統吐屯為人所殺，欲谷設兵又為其俟斤所破，咥利失復得舊地，弩失畢、處密等並歸咥利失。

translations.literal: The supervising tutun was killed by others; Yugu She's army was also broken by his yijin; Xieli Shi recovered his old lands, and Nushibi, Chumi, and others all returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: The tutun was slain; Yugu She's force was routed by his yijin; Xieli Shi regained his territory and Nushibi and Chumi submitted again.

sentences.zh: 十二年，西部竟立欲谷設為乙毗咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the western tribes at last set up Yugu She as Qaghan Yipi Zhuolu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the west enthroned Yugu She as Qaghan Yipi Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 乙毗咄陸可汗既立，與咥利失大戰，兩軍多死，各引去。

translations.literal: Once Qaghan Yipi Zhuolu was established, he fought a great battle with Xieli Shi; both armies suffered heavy losses and each withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yipi Zhuolu and Xieli Shi fought a bloody war and both pulled back.

sentences.zh: 因與咥利失中分，自伊列河已西屬咄陸，已東屬咥利失。

translations.literal: They then divided the realm between them: from the Ili River west belonged to Zhuolu, east to Xieli Shi.
translations.idiomatic: They split the realm at the Ili: west to Zhuolu, east to Xieli Shi.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗又建庭於鏃曷山西，謂為北庭。

translations.literal: Qaghan Zhuolu also built his court west of Mount Cuoha, calling it the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuolu built his court west of Mount Cuoha as the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 自厥越失、拔悉彌、駁馬、結骨、火燅、觸水昆諸國皆臣之。

translations.literal: From Jueyueshi, Basmyl, Boma, Jiegu, Huoxun, and Chushui Kun, every state submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jueyueshi, Basmyl, Boma, Jiegu, Huoxun, Chushui Kun, and others all bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，咥利失為其吐屯俟利發與欲谷設通謀作難，咥利失窮蹙，奔拔汗那而死。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Xieli Shi, pressed by his tutun Jielifa plotting with Yugu She, fled in distress to Ferghana and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year his tutun Jielifa conspired with Yugu She; Xieli Shi fled to Ferghana and died.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢部落酋帥迎咥利失弟伽那之子薄布特勒而立之，是為乙毗沙缽羅葉護可汗。

translations.literal: Nushibi chiefs welcomed Xieli Shi's nephew, the son of Jiana, Bobuteli, and enthroned him as Qaghan Yipi Shaboluo Yehu.
translations.idiomatic: Nushibi leaders enthroned Jiana's son Bobuteli as Qaghan Yipi Shaboluo Yehu.

sentences.zh: 乙毗沙缽羅葉護可汗既立，建庭於睢合水北，謂之南庭。

translations.literal: Once Qaghan Yipi Shaboluo Yehu was established, he built his court north of the Suihe River, calling it the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Yehu built his court north of the Suihe as the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 東以伊列河為界，自龜茲、鄯善，且末、吐火羅、焉耆、石國、史國、何國、穆國、康國，皆受其節度。

translations.literal: East to the Ili River as boundary; from Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tukhara, Yanqi, Shiguo, Shiguo of the Shi, He, Mu, and Kang—all came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Ili lay his domain: Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tukhara, Yanqi, Shiguo, Shi, He, Mu, Kang, and the rest obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 累遣使朝貢，太宗降璽書慰勉。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys with tribute; Taizong sent sealed edicts of comfort and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He sent tribute missions again and again; Taizong answered with imperial letters of praise.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年，令左領軍將軍張大師往授焉，賜以鼓纛。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan he ordered Left Leading General Zhang Dash to go invest him and granted drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 15 Left Leading General Zhang Dash was sent to invest him with drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 於時咄陸可汗與葉護頗相攻擊。

translations.literal: At that time Qaghan Zhuolu and Yehu attacked each other frequently.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuolu and Yehu were fighting fiercely.

sentences.zh: 會咄陸遣使詣闕，太宗諭以敦睦之道。

translations.literal: When Zhuolu sent envoys to court, Taizong instructed them in the way of close kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuolu's envoys were taught the virtues of harmony.

sentences.zh: 咄陸於時兵眾漸強，西域諸國復來歸附。

translations.literal: Zhuolu's forces grew stronger by the day, and the western states again submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His armies swelled and the western states returned to his fold.

sentences.zh: 未幾，咄陸遣石國吐屯攻葉護，擒之，送於咄陸，尋為所殺。

translations.literal: Before long Zhuolu sent the Shiguo tutun to attack Yehu, captured him, and sent him to Zhuolu, who soon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhuolu's Shiguo tutun seized Yehu, delivered him to Zhuolu, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗既並其國，弩失畢諸姓心不服咄陸，皆叛之。

translations.literal: Once Qaghan Zhuolu had annexed his state, the Nushibi clans resented him and all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuolu swallowed Yehu's realm the Nushibi clans rebelled.

sentences.zh: 咄陸復率兵擊吐火羅，破之。

translations.literal: Zhuolu again led troops against Tukhara and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Tukhara and crushed it.

sentences.zh: 自恃其強，專擅西域。

translations.literal: Relying on his strength, he monopolized the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled the west by force alone.

sentences.zh: 遣兵寇伊州，安西都護郭恪率輕騎二千自烏骨邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: He sent troops to raid Yizhou; Protector-General of Anxi Guo Ke led two thousand light horsemen from Wugu to intercept and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: His raiders struck Yizhou; Guo Ke of Anxi ambushed them from Wugu with two thousand light horse and won.

sentences.zh: 咄陸又遣處月、處密等圍天山縣，郭恪又擊走之。

translations.literal: Zhuolu also sent Chuyue and Chumi to besiege Tianshan county; Guo Ke drove them off again.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyue and Chumi besieged Tianshan; Guo Ke repulsed them again.

sentences.zh: 恪乘勝進拔處月俟斤所居之城，追奔及於遏索山，斬首千余級，降其處密之眾而歸。

translations.literal: Ke pressed the victory, stormed the city where the Chuyue yijin dwelt, pursued to Mount Esuo, beheaded more than a thousand, and returned with the surrendered Chumi people.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing to Mount Esuo he took the Chuyue yijin's city, slew over a thousand, and brought the Chumi clans back in submission.

sentences.zh: 咄陸初以泥孰啜自擅取所部物，斬之以徇；

translations.literal: At first Zhuolu had Niqi Chuo seize goods from his own command without leave and executed him as a warning;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuolu once executed Niqi Chuo for seizing booty from his own command.

sentences.zh: 尋為泥孰啜部將胡祿居所襲，眾多亡逸，其國大亂。

translations.literal: Soon he was attacked by Niqi Chuo's officer Hulu Ju; many fled, and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Niqi Chuo's officer Hulu Ju struck him; multitudes fled and the realm collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年，部下屋利啜等謀欲廢咄陸，各遣使詣闕，請立可汗。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan subordinates such as Wuli Chuo plotted to depose Zhuolu; each sent envoys to court requesting a qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 15 Wuli Chuo and others plotted to remove Zhuolu and each asked the court to name a qaghan.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使賫璽書立莫賀咄乙毗可汗之子，是為乙毗射匱可汗。

translations.literal: Taizong sent envoys bearing sealed edicts to set up the son of Qaghan Mohe Duo Yipi, who became Qaghan Yipi Shekui.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's envoys invested Mohe Duo Yipi's son as Qaghan Yipi Shekui.

sentences.zh: 乙毗射匱可汗立，乃發弩失畢兵就白水擊咄陸。

translations.literal: Once Qaghan Yipi Shekui was established, he mobilized Nushibi troops to strike Zhuolu at Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: Shekui rallied Nushibi to attack Zhuolu at Baishui.

sentences.zh: 自知不為眾所附，乃西走吐火羅國。

translations.literal: Knowing he lacked popular support, he fled west to Tukhara.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing he had no following, he fled to Tukhara.

sentences.zh: 中國使人先為咄陸所拘者，射匱悉以禮資送歸長安，復遣使貢方物，請賜婚。

translations.literal: Chinese envoys earlier detained by Zhuolu were all courteously sent back to Chang'an by Shekui; he again sent envoys with local products and requested marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys Zhuolu had held were sent home with honor; Shekui sent tribute and asked for a princess.

sentences.zh: 太宗許之，詔令割龜茲、於闐、疏勒、硃俱波、蔥嶺等五國為聘禮。

translations.literal: Taizong agreed and ordered that Kucha, Khotan, Shule, Zhujubo, and Congling—five states—be given as betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed and allotted Kucha, Khotan, Shule, Zhujubo, and Congling as bride-price.

sentences.zh: 及太宗崩，賀魯反叛，射匱部落為其所並。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Helu rebelled and Shekui's tribes were absorbed by him.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death Helu rebelled and absorbed Shekui's people.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，與其子咥運率眾西遁，據咄陸可汗之地，總有西域諸郡，建牙於雙河及千泉，自號沙缽羅可汗，統攝咄陸、弩失畢十姓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he fled west with his son Zhayun, seized Zhuolu's lands, controlled the western commanderies, set his standards at Shuanghe and the Thousand Springs, styled himself Qaghan Shaboluo, and ruled the Zhuolu and Nushibi ten surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 2 he fled west with Zhayun, took Zhuolu's domain, held the western prefectures, camped at Shuanghe and the Thousand Springs, called himself Qaghan Shaboluo, and ruled the ten surnames.

sentences.zh: 其咄陸有五啜：一曰處木昆律啜；

translations.literal: The Zhuolu had five chuo: first, the Chumukun Lü Chuo;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuolu had five chuo: first the Chumukun Lü chuo;

sentences.zh: 二曰胡祿居闕啜，賀魯以女妻之；

translations.literal: second, the Hulu Ju Que Chuo—Helu gave him his daughter in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: second the Hulu Ju Que chuo, whom Helu married to his daughter;

sentences.zh: 三曰攝舍提暾啜；

translations.literal: third, the She She Ti Dun Chuo;
translations.idiomatic: third the She She Ti Dun chuo;

sentences.zh: 四曰突騎施賀邏施啜；

translations.literal: fourth, the Tuqishi Heluoshi Chuo;
translations.idiomatic: fourth the Tuqishi Heluoshi chuo;

sentences.zh: 五曰鼠尼施處半啜。

translations.literal: fifth, the Shunishi Chuban Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: fifth the Shunishi Chuban chuo.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢有五俟斤：一曰阿悉結闕俟斤，最為強盛；

translations.literal: The Nushibi had five yijin: first, the Asijie Que Yijin, the most powerful;
translations.idiomatic: Nushibi had five yijin: first Asijie Que yijin, the strongest;

sentences.zh: 二曰哥舒闕俟斤；

translations.literal: second, the Geshu Que Yijin;
translations.idiomatic: second Geshu Que yijin;

sentences.zh: 三曰拔塞幹暾沙缽俟斤，四曰阿悉結泥孰俟斤；

translations.literal: third, the Baisaigan Dun Shabo Yijin; fourth, the Asijie Niqi Yijin;
translations.idiomatic: third Baisaigan Dun Shabo yijin; fourth Asijie Niqi yijin;

sentences.zh: 五曰哥舒處半俟斤。

translations.literal: fifth, the Geshu Chuban Yijin.
translations.idiomatic: fifth Geshu Chuban yijin.

sentences.zh: 各有所部，勝兵數十萬，並羈屬賀魯。

translations.literal: Each had his own following; fit warriors numbered hundreds of thousands, all bound to Helu.
translations.idiomatic: Each commanded his own tribes—hundreds of thousands of warriors—all tied to Helu.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國，亦多附隸焉。

translations.literal: The western states for the most part also submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Most western kingdoms bowed to him as well.

sentences.zh: 賀魯尋立咥運為莫賀咄葉護，數侵擾西蕃諸部，又進寇廷州。

translations.literal: Helu soon set up Zhayun as Yehu Mohe Duo and repeatedly raided the western tribes, also advancing to raid Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Helu made Zhayun Yehu Mohe Duo and harried the western tribes, even raiding Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔遣左武候大將軍梁建方、右驍衛大將軍契苾何力率燕然都護所部回紇兵五萬騎討之，前後斬首五千級，虜渠帥六十余人。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict sent Left Martial Guard General Liang Jianfang and Right Martial Guard General Qibi Heli with fifty thousand Uyghur horsemen of the Yanran Protectorate to attack; in successive battles they beheaded five thousand and captured more than sixty chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Liang Jianfang and Qibi Heli led fifty thousand Yanran Uyghur horse, slew five thousand, and took sixty-odd chiefs.

sentences.zh: 四年，咄陸可汗死，其子真珠護與五弩失畢請擊賀魯，破其牙帳，斬首千余級。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Qaghan Zhuolu died; his son Zhenzhu Hu and the five Nushibi asked to strike Helu and smashed his camp, beheading more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Zhuolu died; Zhenzhu Hu and the five Nushibi joined the attack, broke Helu's camp, and took a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，遣右屯衛將軍蘇定方，燕然都護任雅相，副都護蕭嗣業，左驍衛大將軍、瀚海都督回紇婆閏等率師討擊，仍使右武衛大將軍阿史那彌射、左屯衛大將軍阿史那步真為安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he sent Right Tunwei General Su Dingfang, Yanran Protector Ren Yaxiang, Vice Protector Xiao Siye, Left Martial Guard General and Hanhai Commissioner Uyghur Polun, and others; Right Martial Guard General Ashina Mishe and Left Tunwei General Ashina Bozhen were made pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 Su Dingfang, Ren Yaxiang, Xiao Siye, Polun, and others marched; Mishe and Bozhen served as pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 定方行至曳咥河西，賀魯率胡祿居闕啜等二萬余騎列陣而待。

translations.literal: When Dingfang reached west of the Yexi River, Helu arrayed more than twenty thousand horsemen of the Hulu Ju Que Chuo and others to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yexi River Helu drew up over twenty thousand horse of the Hulu Ju Que chuo.

sentences.zh: 定方率副總管任雅相等與之交戰，賊眾大敗，斬大首領都搭達幹等二百余人。

translations.literal: Dingfang with Vice Commander Ren Yaxiang and others joined battle; the rebels were greatly defeated, and more than two hundred great chiefs including Dutadagan were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfang and Ren Yaxiang engaged; the enemy was routed and two hundred chiefs including Dutadagan were killed.

sentences.zh: 賀魯及闕啜輕騎奔竄，渡伊麗河，兵馬溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Helu and the Que Chuo fled on light horse; crossing the Ili River, very many men and horses drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and the Que chuo fled; crossing the Ili, countless men and horses drowned.

sentences.zh: 嗣業至千泉賀魯下牙之處，彌射進軍至伊麗水，處月、處密等部各率眾來降。

translations.literal: Siye reached the place of Helu's camp below the Thousand Springs; Mishe advanced to the Ili waters; the Chuyue and Chumi each led their masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Siye reached Helu's camp at the Thousand Springs; Mishe reached the Ili; Chuyue and Chumi submitted.

sentences.zh: 彌射又進次雙河，賀魯先使步失達幹鳩集散卒，據柵拒戰。

translations.literal: Mishe advanced again to Shuanghe; Helu had first sent Bushidagan to gather scattered troops and hold a palisade to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At Shuanghe Helu's Bushidagan held a stockade with remnant troops.

sentences.zh: 彌射、步真攻之，大潰；

translations.literal: Mishe and Bozhen attacked and broke them completely;
translations.idiomatic: Mishe and Bozhen stormed it and shattered the defense;

sentences.zh: 又與蘇定方攻賀魯於碎葉水，大破之。

translations.literal: they again joined Su Dingfang to attack Helu at the Suyab River and defeated him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: then with Su Dingfang they crushed Helu at the Suyab River.

sentences.zh: 賀魯與咥運欲投鼠耨設，至石國之蘇咄城傍，人馬饑乏，城主伊涅達幹詐將酒食出迎，賀魯信其言入城，遂被拘執。

translations.literal: Helu and Zhayun meant to flee to the Shunishi She; reaching beside the Sudu city of Shiguo, men and horses were hungry and exhausted; the lord Yiniedagan feigned welcome with food and drink; Helu trusted his words and entered the city, and was then seized.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and Zhayun sought the Shunishi She; at Shiguo's Sudu city, starving, they trusted lord Yiniedagan's feast and were seized in the city.

sentences.zh: 蕭嗣業既至石國，鼠耨設乃以賀魯屬之。

translations.literal: When Siye reached Shiguo, the Shunishi She then handed Helu over to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Siye arrived the Shunishi She delivered Helu to him.

sentences.zh: 賀魯謂嗣業曰：「我破亡虜耳！

translations.literal: Helu said to Siye: "I am a broken fugitive!
translations.idiomatic: Helu told Siye: "I am a ruined captive!

sentences.zh: 先帝厚我，而我背之，今日之敗，天怒我也。

translations.literal: The late emperor treated me generously, yet I betrayed him; today's defeat is Heaven's anger at me.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor favored me and I betrayed him; this defeat is Heaven's wrath.

sentences.zh: 舊聞漢法，殺人皆於都市，至京殺我，請向昭陵，使得謝罪於先帝，是本願也。

translations.literal: I have heard Han law: executions are in the market; if I am to be killed in the capital, I beg to face Zhaoling so I may confess my crime to the late emperor—that is my true wish.
translations.idiomatic: I know Tang law kills at the capital; if I must die, let me bow at Zhaoling to the late emperor—that is my wish.

sentences.zh: 」高宗聞而湣之。

translations.literal: When Gaozong heard this he pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 及俘賀魯至京師，令獻於昭陵及太廟，詔特免死。

translations.literal: When the captive Helu reached the capital, he was presented at Zhaoling and the Imperial Ancestors; an edict specially spared his life.
translations.idiomatic: Brought to the capital he was presented at Zhaoling and the Ancestral Temple; an edict spared his life.

sentences.zh: 分其種落置昆陵、濛池二都護府，其所役屬諸國，皆分置州府，西盡於波斯，並隸安西都護府。

translations.literal: His tribes were placed in the Kunling and Mengchi protectorates; the states he had ruled were each given prefectures and counties; west to Persia all were under the Anxi Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: His tribes went to Kunling and Mengchi protectorates; subject states became prefectures west to Persia under Anxi.

sentences.zh: 四年，賀魯卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Helu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Helu died.

sentences.zh: 詔葬於頡利墓側，刻石以紀其事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered burial beside Jieli's tomb with stone carved to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried beside Jieli's tomb with an inscribed stone.

sentences.zh: 阿史那彌射者，室點密可汗五代孫也。

translations.literal: Ashina Mishe was the fifth-generation descendant of Qaghan Shimi Dian.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Mishe was five generations from Qaghan Shimi Dian.

sentences.zh: 初，室點密從單於統領十大首領，有兵十萬眾，往平西域諸胡國，自為可汗，號十姓部落，世統其眾。

translations.literal: At first Shimi Dian followed the Shanyu in commanding the ten great chiefs, with an army of a hundred thousand; he went to pacify the western Hu states, made himself qaghan, styled the Ten Surname Tribes, and his line ruled the masses for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Shimi Dian had led a hundred thousand men to pacify the west, made himself qaghan of the Ten Surnames, and his line ruled for generations.

sentences.zh: 彌射在本蕃為莫賀咄葉護。

translations.literal: Mishe in his homeland was Yehu Mohe Duo.
translations.idiomatic: At home Mishe had been Yehu Mohe Duo.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，詔遣鴻臚少卿劉善因就蕃立為奚利邲咄陸可汗，賜以鼓纛、彩帛萬段。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan an edict sent Vice Director Liu Shanyin to his tribe to invest him as Qaghan Xili Zhuolu, granting drums, banners, and ten thousand bolts of silks.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 6 Liu Shanyin invested him Qaghan Xili Zhuolu with drums, banners, and ten thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其族兄步真欲自立為可汗，遂謀殺彌射弟侄二十余人。

translations.literal: His clansman Bozhen wished to make himself qaghan and plotted to kill more than twenty of Mishe's younger brothers and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Bozhen sought the throne and murdered more than twenty of Mishe's kin.

sentences.zh: 彌射既與步真有隙，以貞觀十三年率所部處月、處密部落入朝，授右監門大將軍。

translations.literal: Mishe, at odds with Bozhen, in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan led his Chuyue and Chumi tribes to court and was appointed General of the Right Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Estranged from Bozhen, in Zhenguan 13 Mishe led Chuyue and Chumi to court and became General of the Right Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 其後步真遂自立為咄陸葉護，其部落多不服，委之遁去。

translations.literal: Later Bozhen made himself Zhuolu Yehu; many of his tribes would not obey and deserted him.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen then styled himself Zhuolu Yehu; many tribes deserted.

sentences.zh: 步真復攜家屬入朝，授左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Bozhen again brought his household to court and was appointed Left Tunwei General.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen came to court with his family and was made Left Tunwei General.

sentences.zh: 彌射後從太宗征高麗有功，封平襄縣伯。

translations.literal: Mishe later followed Taizong against Goguryeo with merit and was enfeoffed Baron of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Mishe later served on the Goguryeo campaign and was made Baron of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，轉右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was transferred to General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 he became General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 及討平賀魯，乃冊立彌射為興昔亡可汗兼右衛大將軍、昆陵都護，分押賀魯下五咄六部落。

translations.literal: When Helu was pacified, Mishe was invested Qaghan Xingxiwang and concurrently General of the Right Guard and Protector-General of Kunling, holding the five Zhuolu tribes under Helu.
translations.idiomatic: After Helu's defeat Mishe was named Qaghan Xingxiwang, Right Guard General, Kunling Protector, over the five Zhuolu tribes.

sentences.zh: 步真授繼往絕可汗，兼右衛大將軍、濛池都護，仍分押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: Bozhen was given Qaghan Jiwangjue and concurrently Right Guard General and Mengchi Protector, still holding the five Nushibi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen became Qaghan Jiwangjue, Right Guard General, Mengchi Protector, over the five Nushibi tribes.

sentences.zh: 因下詔曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed, saying:

sentences.zh: 自西蕃罹亂，三十余年。

translations.literal: Since the western barbarians suffered disorder, more than thirty years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: The western lands have known turmoil for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 比者賀魯猖狂，百姓重被劫掠。

translations.literal: Recently Helu ran wild and the common people were again plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Helu's rampages have ravaged the people anew.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨四海，情均養育。

translations.literal: I rule the four seas with equal care in nurture.
translations.idiomatic: I rule all beneath Heaven and would nurture all alike.

sentences.zh: 不可使兇狡之虜，恣行侵漁，無辜之氓，久遭塗炭。

translations.literal: I cannot let fierce and cunning barbarians wantonly raid and plunder, nor innocent folk long suffer ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I will not let the cruel prey on the innocent any longer.

sentences.zh: 故遣右屯衛將軍蘇定方等統率騎勇，北路討逐。

translations.literal: Therefore I sent Right Tunwei General Su Dingfang and others to lead cavalry north to pursue and drive them out.
translations.idiomatic: I sent Su Dingfang and others north with cavalry to hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 卿等宣暢朝風，南道撫育。

translations.literal: You shall proclaim the court's grace and comfort the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: You will carry the court's kindness along the southern road.

sentences.zh: 遂使兇渠畏威，夷人慕德，伐叛柔服，西域總平。

translations.literal: Thus the fierce chieftains feared our might, the barbarians admired our virtue; rebels were punished and the submissive comforted, and the Western Regions were altogether pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were broken, the willing embraced, and the west was pacified.

sentences.zh: 賀魯父子既已擒獲，諸頭部落須有統領。

translations.literal: Helu and his son are captured; the tribal heads must have leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and his son are prisoners; the tribes need leaders.

sentences.zh: 卿早歸闕庭，久參宿衛，深感恩義，甚知法式，所以冊立卿等各為一部可汗。

translations.literal: You returned early to the court, long served in the guard, deeply know grace and duty, and well understand law and form—therefore I invest each of you qaghan over a division.
translations.idiomatic: You know Tang law and loyalty; I name each of you qaghan over a division.

sentences.zh: 但諸姓從賀魯，非其本情，卿等才至即降，亦是赤心向國。

translations.literal: But the clans followed Helu against their true will; you won them the moment you arrived—that too is loyal hearts toward the state.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Helu unwillingly; your arrival won them—that is loyalty to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 卿宜與盧承慶等準其部落大小，位望高下，節級授刺史以下官。

translations.literal: You should with Lu Chengqing and others, according to each tribe's size and each chief's standing, grant officials from cishi downward as befits their rank.
translations.idiomatic: With Lu Chengqing, grant prefects and lower ranks according to each tribe's size and standing.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，又令彌射、步真率所部從釭海道大總管蘇海政討龜茲。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo era he again ordered Mishe and Bozhen to lead their commands with Grand Commander Su Haizheng of the Gang Sea route against Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo Mishe and Bozhen joined Grand Commander Su Haizheng against Kucha.

sentences.zh: 步真嘗欲並彌射部落，遂密告海政云：「彌射欲謀反，請以計誅之。

translations.literal: Bozhen had long wished to absorb Mishe's tribes and secretly told Haizheng: "Mishe plans rebellion; please use a stratagem to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen coveted Mishe's tribes and whispered to Haizheng: "Mishe plots rebellion—kill him by trickery.

sentences.zh: 」時海政兵才數千，懸師在彌射境內，遂集軍吏而謀曰：「彌射若反，我輩即無噍類。

translations.literal: At that time Haizheng had only a few thousand troops, deep in Mishe's territory; he gathered his officers and said: "If Mishe rebels, we shall have nothing to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Haizheng had only thousands of men inside Mishe's land; his officers said: "If he rebels we perish.

sentences.zh: 今宜先舉事，則可克捷。

translations.literal: We should strike first, then we can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: We must strike first to survive.

sentences.zh: 」乃偽稱有敕，令大總管賫物數百萬段分賜可汗及諸首領。

translations.literal: He then falsely claimed an edict, ordering the grand commander to distribute several million bolts of goods among the qaghan and chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: He forged an edict promising millions of bolts of goods to qaghan and chiefs.

sentences.zh: 由是彌射率其麾下，隨例請物，海政盡收斬之。

translations.literal: Mishe therefore led his followers to request shares by precedent; Haizheng seized and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Mishe and his men came to claim their share; Haizheng seized and slaughtered them all.

sentences.zh: 共後西蕃盛言彌射非反，為步真所誣，而海政不能審察，濫行誅戮。

translations.literal: Afterward the western tribes widely said Mishe had not rebelled but was slandered by Bozhen, while Haizheng could not investigate and wantonly executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the west insisted Mishe was framed by Bozhen and wrongly slaughtered by Haizheng.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，十姓無主數年，部落多散失。

translations.literal: When Wu Zetian held court, the ten surnames lacked leaders for several years and many tribes scattered and were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wu Zetian the ten surnames went leaderless for years and tribes dispersed.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，遂擢授彌射子左豹韜衛翊府中郎將元慶為左玉鈐衛將軍兼昆陵都護，令襲興昔亡可汗，押五咄六部落。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong he promoted Mishe son, Central Gentleman of the Left Leopard-Bow Guard Yifu Zhonglang Jiang Yuanqing, to General of the Left Jade Bell Guard and concurrent Protector-General of Kunling, ordering him to succeed Qaghan Xingxiwang and hold the five Zhuolu tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In early Chuigong Yuanqing, Mishe son, was made Kunling Protector and Qaghan Xingxiwang over the five Zhuolu.

sentences.zh: 步真子斛瑟羅為右玉鈐衛將軍，兼濛池都護，押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: Bozhen son Husiluo was made General of the Right Jade Bell Guard and concurrent Protector-General of Mengchi, holding the five Nushibi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen son Husiluo became Mengchi Protector over the five Nushibi.

sentences.zh: 尋進授元慶左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon Yuanqing was advanced to General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing was soon promoted General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 突騎施烏質勒者，西突厥之別種也。

translations.literal: Wuzhile of the Tuqishi was a separate branch of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile of the Tuqishi was a Western Turk offshoot.

sentences.zh: 初隸在斛瑟羅下，號為莫賀達幹。

translations.literal: At first he was subordinate to Husiluo and styled Mohe Daghan.
translations.idiomatic: He first served under Husiluo as Mohe Daghan.

sentences.zh: 後以斛瑟羅用刑嚴酷，眾皆畏之，尤能撫恤其部落，由是為遠近諸胡所歸附。

translations.literal: Later, because Husiluo punishments were harsh and all feared him, yet Wuzhile was especially able to comfort his tribes, for this reason the distant Hu peoples far and near submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Husiluo ruled cruelly and inspired fear, but Wuzhile won his tribes and drew distant Hu peoples to his banner.

sentences.zh: 其下置都督二十員，各統兵七千人。

translations.literal: Below him he placed twenty commissioners, each commanding seven thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed twenty commissioners, each with seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 嘗屯聚碎葉西北界，後漸攻陷碎葉，徙其牙帳居之。

translations.literal: He once camped on the northwest border of Suyab; later he gradually attacked and took Suyab and moved his standards to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: He camped northwest of Suyab, then seized the city and moved his court there.

sentences.zh: 東北與突厥為鄰，西南與諸胡相接，東南至西廷州。

translations.literal: Northeast he bordered the Turks; southwest he connected with the various Hu; southeast to Xiting prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast lay the Turks, to the southwest the Hu states, to the southeast Xiting.

sentences.zh: 斛瑟羅以部眾削弱，自則天時入朝，不敢還蕃，其地並為烏質勒所並。

translations.literal: Husiluo, as his followers grew weak, from Wu Zetian time entered court and dared not return to his tribe; his lands were all absorbed by Wuzhile.
translations.idiomatic: Husiluo power waned; from Wu Zetian reign he stayed at court and Wuzhile absorbed his lands.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，詔封為西河郡王，令攝御史大夫，解琬就加冊立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong an edict enfeoffed him Prince of Xihe commandery, ordered him to act as Censor-in-Chief, and Jie Wan went to invest him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 2 he was made Prince of Xihe and acting Censor-in-Chief; Jie Wan was sent to invest him.

sentences.zh: 未至，烏質勒卒。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Wuzhile died.
translations.idiomatic: Before Jie Wan arrived, Wuzhile died.

sentences.zh: 其長子娑葛代統其眾，詔便立娑葛為金河郡王，仍賜以宮女四人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Suoge succeeded to his following; an edict at once established Suoge as Prince of Jinhe commandery and still granted four palace women.
translations.idiomatic: His son Suoge took command; the court made him Prince of Jinhe and gave him four palace women.

sentences.zh: 初，娑葛代父統兵，烏質勒下部將闕啜忠節甚忌之，以兵部尚書宗楚客當朝任勢，密遣使賫金七百兩以賂楚客，請停娑葛統兵。

translations.literal: At first, when Suoge succeeded his father in command, Wuzhile subordinate general Quechuo Zhongjie greatly resented him; because Minister of War Zong Chuke held power at court, he secretly sent envoys with seven hundred taels of gold to bribe Chuke, requesting that Suoge be stopped from commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge rise angered Zhongjie, a Wuzhile officer; he bribed the powerful Zong Chuke with seven hundred taels of gold to strip Suoge of command.

sentences.zh: 楚客乃遣御史中丞馮嘉賓充使至其境，陰與忠節籌其事，並自致書以申意。

translations.literal: Chuke then sent Vice Censor Feng Jiabin as envoy to his territory, secretly plotting the affair with Zhongjie, and also sent a letter in his own hand to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke sent Vice Censor Feng Jiabin to plot with Zhongjie and wrote to confirm the scheme.

sentences.zh: 在路為娑葛遊兵所獲，遂斬嘉賓，仍進兵攻陷火燒等城，遣使上表以索楚客頭。

translations.literal: On the road he was seized by Suoge patrol troops; Suoge then beheaded Jiabin, advanced to capture the cities of Huoshao and others, and sent a memorial demanding Chuke head.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge patrols captured Jiabin and beheaded him, took Huoshao and other cities, and demanded Chuke head by memorial.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，娑葛弟遮弩恨所分部落少於其兄，遂叛入突厥，請為鄉導，以討娑葛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong Suoge younger brother Zhenu, resenting that his allotted tribes were fewer than his brother, rebelled and entered the Turks, requesting to be a guide to attack Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 3 his brother Zhenu, given fewer tribes, defected to the Turks as a guide against Suoge.

sentences.zh: 默啜乃留遮弩，遣兵二萬人與其左右來討娑葛，擒之而還。

translations.literal: Mochuo then detained Zhenu and sent twenty thousand troops with his attendants to attack Suoge, captured him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo held Zhenu and sent twenty thousand men to capture Suoge.

sentences.zh: 默啜顧謂遮弩曰：「汝於兄弟尚不和協，豈能盡心於我。

translations.literal: Mochuo then said to Zhenu: "You cannot even harmonize with your brothers—how can you devote yourself fully to me?
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo told Zhenu: "You cannot keep peace with your own brother—how will you serve me faithfully?

sentences.zh: 」遂與娑葛俱殺之。

translations.literal: He then killed both together with Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Zhenu and Suoge together.

sentences.zh: 默啜兵還，娑葛下部將蘇祿鳩集余眾，自立為可汗。

translations.literal: When Mochuo army returned, Suoge subordinate general Suluku gathered the remnant masses and set himself up as qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: After Mochuo withdrew, Suluku rallied the remnants and made himself qaghan.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿者，突騎施別種也。

translations.literal: Suluku was also a separate branch of the Tuqishi.
translations.idiomatic: Suluku too was a Tuqishi offshoot.

sentences.zh: 頗善綏撫，十姓部落漸歸附之，眾二十萬，遂雄西域之地，尋遣使來朝。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled in soothing and comforting; the ten-surname tribes gradually submitted to him; his masses numbered two hundred thousand; he soon dominated the lands of the Western Regions and sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at winning hearts, he drew the ten surnames until two hundred thousand strong, dominated the west, and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，制授蘇祿為左羽林軍大將軍、金方道經略大使，進為特勒，遣侍御史解忠順賫璽書冊立為忠順可汗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan by decree he was appointed General of the Left Forest Army and Commissioner of the Jinfang Circuit, advanced to tegin; Attending Censor Jie Zhongshun was sent bearing sealed edicts to invest him as Qaghan Zhongshun.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 3 he became Left Forest General and Jinfang commissioner, then tegin; Jie Zhongshun invested him Qaghan Zhongshun.

sentences.zh: 自是每年遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: From then on each year he sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Each year thereafter he sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 上乃立史懷道女為金河公主以妻之。

translations.literal: The emperor then established the daughter of Shi Huaidao as Princess Jinhe to marry him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave Shi Huaidao daughter as Princess Jinhe in marriage.

sentences.zh: 時杜暹為安西都護，公主遣牙官賫馬千疋詣安西互市。

translations.literal: At that time Du Xian was Protector-General of Anxi; the princess sent a tooth officer with a thousand horses to Anxi for trade.
translations.idiomatic: Du Xian was Anxi Protector; the princess sent an officer with a thousand horses to trade at Anxi.

sentences.zh: 使者宣公主教與暹，暹怒曰：「阿史那氏女，豈合宣教與吾節度耶！

translations.literal: The envoy proclaimed the princess command to Xian; Xian angrily said: "A daughter of the Ashina clan—how is it fitting that she proclaim commands to my commandery!
translations.idiomatic: The envoy announced the princess orders; Xian raged: "An Ashina woman has no right to command a Tang frontier general!

sentences.zh: 」杖其使者，留而不遣，其馬經雪，寒死並盡。

translations.literal: He flogged the envoy and detained him without release; the horses, passing through snow, died of cold, all perishing.
translations.idiomatic: He whipped the envoy and held him; the horses perished in the snow.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿大怒，發兵分寇四鎮。

translations.literal: Suluku was greatly angered and sent troops in divisions to raid the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Suluku sent armies against all Four Garrisons.

sentences.zh: 會杜暹入知政事，趙頤貞代為安西都護，城守久之，由是四鎮貯積及人畜並為蘇祿所掠，安西僅全。

translations.literal: When Xian entered court to take part in governance, Zhao Yizhen replaced him as Anxi Protector; they held the cities for a long time; thereby the stored goods, livestock, and people of the Four Garrisons were all plundered by Suluku; only Anxi itself was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Xian left for Chang'an; Zhao Yizhen held on, but stores and herds were looted—only the garrison towns survived.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿既聞杜暹入相，稍引退，俄又遣使入朝獻方物。

translations.literal: When Suluku heard Xian had entered the phase, he drew back somewhat; soon he again sent envoys to court with local products.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Xian was chancellor, Suluku pulled back and soon sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 十八年，蘇祿使至京師，玄宗禦丹鳳樓設宴。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Suluku envoys reached the capital; Xuanzong held a feast at Danfeng Tower.
translations.idiomatic: In year 18 his envoys came; Xuanzong feasted them at Danfeng Tower.

sentences.zh: 突厥先遣使入朝，是日亦來預宴，與蘇祿使爭長。

translations.literal: The Turks had first sent envoys to court; that day they also came to the feast and disputed precedence with Suluku envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Turk envoys already at court also attended and quarreled over seating with Suluku men.

sentences.zh: 突厥使曰：「突騎施國小，本是突厥之臣，不宜居上。

translations.literal: The Turk envoy said: "The Tuqishi state is small and was originally a subject of the Turks—it is not fitting to sit above.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk envoy said: "Tuqishi is small and was our vassal—you should not sit above us.

sentences.zh: 」蘇祿使曰：「今日此宴，乃為我設，不合居下。

translations.literal: Suluku envoy said: "Today this feast was arranged for me—it is not fitting to sit below.
translations.idiomatic: Suluku envoy replied: "This feast is for us—we will not sit below.

sentences.zh: 」於是中書門下及百僚議，遂於東西幕下兩處分坐，突厥使在東，突騎施使在西。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat-Chancellery and the hundred officials deliberated and finally seated them in two places under east and west canopies—the Turk envoy in the east, the Tuqishi envoy in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The court seated them separately—Turks east, Tuqishi west.

sentences.zh: 宴訖，厚賫而遣之。

translations.literal: When the feast ended, they were richly rewarded and sent off.
translations.idiomatic: They were richly rewarded and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿性尤清儉，每戰伐，有所克獲，盡分與將士及諸部落。

translations.literal: Suluku was especially frugal and clear; whenever he fought and gained booty, he divided it all among his generals and the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Suluku was austere; every victory spoils went to his officers and tribes.

sentences.zh: 其下愛之，甚為其用。

translations.literal: His followers loved him and served him devotedly.
translations.idiomatic: His men loved him and fought willingly for him.

sentences.zh: 潛又遣使南通吐蕃，東附突厥。

translations.literal: Secretly he also sent envoys south to Tibet and east to attach himself to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly allied with Tibet and the Turks.

sentences.zh: 突厥及吐蕃亦嫁女與蘇祿。

translations.literal: The Turks and Tibet also gave daughters to Suluku in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Turks and Tibetans both married daughters to him.

sentences.zh: 既以三國女為可敦，又分立數子為葉護，費用漸廣。

translations.literal: Having three states daughters as katuns, he also set up several sons as yabghu; expenses gradually grew vast.
translations.idiomatic: With three royal wives and many sons made yabghu, his costs soared.

sentences.zh: 先既不為積貯，晚年抄掠所得者，留不分之。

translations.literal: Earlier he had made no stores; in his later years what he gained by raiding he kept and did not divide.
translations.idiomatic: He had never saved; in old age he hoarded plunder instead of sharing.

sentences.zh: 又因風病，一手攣縮，其下諸部，心始攜貳。

translations.literal: Also because of wind disease one hand was contracted and withered; his subordinate tribes began to waver in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wind disease crippled one hand, and his tribes began to turn away.

sentences.zh: 有大首領莫賀達幹、都摩度兩部落，最為強盛。

translations.literal: The great chiefs Mohe Daghan and Dumodu—two tribes—were the most powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs Mohe Daghan and Dumodu led the strongest tribes.

sentences.zh: 百姓又分為黃姓、黑姓兩種，互相猜阻。

translations.literal: The common people were also divided into Yellow Surname and Black Surname, mutually suspicious and obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: His people split into Yellow and Black surnames, bitterly divided.

sentences.zh: 二十六年夏，莫賀達幹勒兵夜攻蘇祿，殺之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year Mohe Daghan led troops by night to attack Suluku and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year 26 Mohe Daghan ambushed and killed Suluku.

sentences.zh: 都摩度初與莫賀達幹連謀，俄又相背，立蘇祿之子咄火仙為可汗，以輯其余眾，與莫賀達幹自相攻擊。

translations.literal: Dumodu at first joined Mohe Daghan in the plot, but soon turned against him, set up Suluku son Tuohuoxian as qaghan to gather the remnant masses, and fought Mohe Daghan.
translations.idiomatic: Dumodu first aided the coup, then backed Suluku son Tuohuoxian and warred with Mohe Daghan.

sentences.zh: 莫賀達幹遣使告安西都護蓋嘉運。

translations.literal: Mohe Daghan sent envoys to inform Anxi Protector Gai Jiayun.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe Daghan appealed to Anxi Protector Gai Jiayun.

sentences.zh: 嘉運率兵討之，大敗都摩度之眾，臨陣擒咄火仙，並收得金河公主而還。

translations.literal: Jiayun led troops to attack and greatly defeated Dumodu masses; on the field he captured Tuohuoxian and also recovered Princess Jinhe and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun routed Dumodu, captured Tuohuoxian, and brought back Princess Jinhe.

sentences.zh: 又欲立史懷道之子昕為可汗以鎮撫之，莫賀達幹不肯，曰：「討平蘇祿，本是我之元謀，若立史昕為主，則國家何以酬賞於我？

translations.literal: He also wished to set up Shi Huaidao son Xin as qaghan to pacify them; Mohe Daghan would not agree, saying: "Suppressing Suluku was originally my chief plan; if Shi Xin is set up as lord, how will the state reward me?
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun meant to install Shi Xin as qaghan; Mohe Daghan refused: "I overthrew Suluku—why reward another man?

sentences.zh: 」乃不立史昕，便令莫賀達幹統眾。

translations.literal: He therefore did not set up Shi Xin but ordered Mohe Daghan to command the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xin was passed over and Mohe Daghan took command.

sentences.zh: 二十七年二月，嘉運率將士詣闕獻俘，玄宗禦花萼樓以宴之，仍令將吐火仙獻於太廟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year Jiayun led officers and soldiers to court to present captives; Xuanzong held a feast at the Hua e Tower and ordered Tuohuoxian presented at the Imperial Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: In month 2 of year 27 Jiayun presented captives at court; Xuanzong feasted him at Hua e Tower and offered Tuohuoxian at the Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 俄又黃姓、黑姓自相屠殺，各遣使降附。

translations.literal: Soon the Yellow and Black surnames slaughtered one another and each sent envoys to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yellow and Black surnames massacred each other and both sought Tang protection.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：中原多事，外國窺邊，周獫狁、漢匈奴之後，其類實繁，前史論之備矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: When the central plains had many troubles, foreign states peered at the borders; after the Xianyun of Zhou and the Xiongnu of Han, their kind was truly numerous—the former histories discuss them fully.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When China was troubled, border peoples watched for weakness; after Zhou Xianyun and Han Xiongnu, their kind multiplied—earlier histories tell it all.

sentences.zh: 突厥自隋文修王道，肅軍容，示恩威以羈縻之；

translations.literal: From the time the Turks cultivated the kingly way under Emperor Wen of Sui, disciplined military appearance, and showed grace and might to keep them on reins—
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Wendi the Turks were bound by disciplined armies and measured grace and might;

sentences.zh: 煬帝失政教，生戎心，肇亂離以啟發之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang lost proper government and teaching, bred a barbarian heart, and began disorder and separation to rouse them.
translations.idiomatic: Yangdi lost the way, stirred their warlike hearts, and loosed chaos upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 高祖借其力而入平京師，群賊附其強而叠據河朔。

translations.literal: Gaozu borrowed their strength to enter and pacify the capital; bandits attached to their might and piled up holdings in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rode their strength into Chang'an; rebels in Hebei clung to their power.

sentences.zh: 高祖同禦榻以延其使，太宗幸便橋以約其和。

translations.literal: Gaozu shared the imperial couch to extend their envoys; Taizong visited Bian Bridge to covenant their peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu received their envoys on the imperial couch; Taizong sealed peace at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 當其時焉，不其盛矣！

translations.literal: In those times—was it not their zenith!
translations.idiomatic: In those days their glory seemed complete!

sentences.zh: 竟滅其族而身死於國者，何也？

translations.literal: Yet in the end their clans were extinguished and they died within the state—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet their clans were destroyed and their khans died in Tang lands—why?

sentences.zh: 咸謂太宗有馭夷狄之道，李勣著戡定之功。

translations.literal: All said Taizong had the way to control barbarians and Li Jing wrote the merit of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Men credit Taizong's mastery of barbarians and Li Jing's conquest.

sentences.zh: 殊不知突厥之始也，賞罰明而將士戮力。

translations.literal: They little knew that at the Turks beginning rewards and punishments were clear and officers and soldiers strove together.
translations.idiomatic: They forget that early Turks ruled by clear reward and united arms.

sentences.zh: 遇煬帝之亂，亡命蓄怒者既附之，其興也宜哉！

translations.literal: Meeting Emperor Yang disorder, fugitives storing wrath all attached to them—their rise was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: When Yangdi's realm collapsed, every fugitive warrior joined them—their rise was inevitable!

sentences.zh: 頡利之衰也，兄弟扌勾隙而部族離心。

translations.literal: When Jieli declined, brothers feuded and tribes lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli fell, brothers fought and tribes deserted.

sentences.zh: 當太宗之理，謀臣猛將討逐之，其亡也宜哉！

translations.literal: Under Taizong ordering, plotting ministers and fierce generals pursued and drove them—their fall was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong, Tang strategists hunted them down—their fall was inevitable!

sentences.zh: 洎武後亂朝，默啜犯塞，玄宗纂嗣，傳首京師，東封太山，西戎扈蹕，開元之代，繼踵來降。

translations.literal: Down to Empress Wu troubled court Mochuo raided the frontier; Xuanzong succeeded and Helu head reached the capital; at Mount Tai in the east the western barbarians escorted the carriage; in the Kaiyuan era submission followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Through Wu Zetian's turmoil and Mochuo's raids, Xuanzong brought Helu's head to Chang'an; western peoples attended his Feng and Shan; Kaiyuan saw endless submissions.

sentences.zh: 西突厥諸族，遇其理，則眾心悅附而甲兵興焉；

translations.literal: The clans of the Western Turks—when they met good order, all hearts gladly attached and armor flourished;
translations.idiomatic: Western Turk clans prospered under good rule and rallied to arms;

sentences.zh: 遇其亂，則族類怨怒而本根破矣！

translations.literal: when they met disorder, tribes resented in anger and the root was broken!
translations.idiomatic: under chaos they turned on one another and their root was severed!

sentences.zh: 理亂二道，華夷一途。

translations.literal: The two paths of order and disorder are one road for Chinese and barbarian alike.
translations.idiomatic: Order and chaos follow one law for Chinese and barbarian alike.

sentences.zh: 或質言於盛衰倚伏，未為確論。

translations.literal: To speak plainly of rise and fall leaning on hidden forces is not yet a sure argument.
translations.idiomatic: Simple talk of fate and fortune is not proof enough.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：中國失政，邊夷幸災。

translations.literal: Comment: When China loses good government, frontier barbarians seize the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: When the center fails, the border peoples seize their chance.

sentences.zh: 理亂之道，取鑒將來。

translations.literal: The way of order and disorder—take it as a mirror for what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Let order and disorder be the mirror for ages yet to come.
